Dear Sir/Madam

Re: Ms Sally McConville, aged 38



I am writing to (urgent=urgently) refer Ms McCnoville, whose symptoms and signs are suggestive of
acute asthma and possible pneumonia. Your (acute=elete) management and assessment would be
(valued.=appreciated)



On today’s visit, Ms McConville presented with deteriorating shortness of breath (and bad general
condition=delete). In spite of(=? I don’t understand what you mean here), prednisolone and antibiotics
were received. A respiratory rate of 25, BP of 100/65, pulse of 112, and temperature of 37.7 were
recorded upon her evaluation.( By inspection=delete) shortness of breath at rest and excessive use of
accessory muscles were noticed. Additionally, (wheeze all over the chest=she was wheezing) and
bilateral basal crepitations were (auscultated=delete?). Ventolin nebules, 5mg was added.



On 12/09/2014, Ms McConville (came to my clinic with a 4=resented with a four)-day history of viral
upper respiratory tract infection(, whose symptoms was progressive=with progressive symptoms). On
further discussion, wheeze over last 24 hours coincide(d) with dyspnea on minimal exertion were
mentioned. (A part =Apart) from congested throat, no abnormalities were detected. (An=delete)
amoxicillin, 500mg ; prednisolone, 25mg three times daily were prescribed, along with (continuing her)
ventolin inhaler (and preventer were continuing.=delete)



Ms McCnoville has a history of asthma, she takes fluticasone, 250 – 2 puffs daily and salbutamol – 2 puffs
if required. (She has no allergy or smoking.=delete)



If you have any queries, do not hesitate to contact me.



Yours faithfully

Doctor
